title: The unlabelled bridge-addable fragment-size conjecture
source: Colin McDiarmid, “Connectivity for an unlabelled bridge-addable graph class”, arXiv:2001.05256 (2020). (https://arxiv.org/abs/2001.05256), Conjecture 3
statement:
Let $\mathcal A$ be a class of graphs that is **bridge-addable**, meaning that adding an edge between vertices in distinct components preserves membership, and **decomposable**, meaning that a graph belongs to $\mathcal A$ if and only if each of its components does. For a graph $G$, define its **fragment size** by

$$
\operatorname{frag}(G)=|V(G)|-\max\{|V(C)|:C\text{ is a component of }G\}.
$$

Let $\tilde{R}_n \in_u\tilde{\mathcal A}$ be sampled uniformly from the unlabelled graphs in $\mathcal A$ on $n$ vertices. **Unlabelled bridge-addable fragment-size conjecture.** For each such graph class $\mathcal A$, there is a constant $c_{\mathcal A}$ such that, for each positive integer $n$,

$$
\mathbb E[\operatorname{frag}(\tilde{R}_n)]\leq c_{\mathcal A}.
$$

The labelled analogue has a uniform expectation bound, while the source gives an unlabelled example showing that the expectation can grow linearly for a particular class; the conjectured bound remains open in general.
summary: McDiarmid's Conjecture 3 (the expected fragment size of a uniformly random unlabelled n-vertex graph from a decomposable, bridge-addable class is bounded by a universal constant) is false: there is one fixed isomorphism-invariant, decomposable, bridge-addable class of graphs, with members at every positive order, whose mean fragment size over isomorphism classes of n-vertex members is unbounded in n. The class consists of graphs whose bridgeless pieces are single vertices or members of a staged family of cyclic-layer graphs with very many isomorphism types; the bound obtained is of order t^2/6 at stage t. The first stage begins at about 2^86 vertices, so the effect is invisible at any computable size (below 2^85 vertices the class is exactly the forests).
paste_summary: Refuted. There is a single decomposable, bridge-addable class of graphs, nonempty at every order, for which the mean fragment size under uniform sampling of unlabelled n-vertex members is unbounded. This contradicts Conjecture 3 of McDiarmid, arXiv:2001.05256. The class is built from a staged family of bridgeless cyclic-layer graphs with very many isomorphism types.
caveat: The formalized class differs in detail from the one in the discovery proof (the paper proves the formalized one; an independent referee re-derived every inequality). The first stage starts near 2^86 vertices, so no direct numerical confirmation at true size is possible; scaled-down copies were checked. The same class refutes the sibling record MathDB 345191 (Conjecture 4), which is not claimed separately. Bounded literature search; both papers citing the source treat the unlabelled conjectures as open.
